title: Correct shard-offset misalignment causing transient double-counts in per-model streaming charts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Symptoms: Some customers reported short-lived spikes in per-model token/usage charts after ingestion backfills and rate-limit retries. Spikes appear only for models using the new sharded rate limiter (shard-epoching enabled) and occur during backfill windows or after delayed streaming events. Impact: transient double-counts in the Console charts and alerting noise; can result in incorrect chargeable aggregation for short windows and confuses SRE oncall. Scope: affects hosted API ingestion that routes events through the sharded token-tally pipeline when (a) events arrive out-of-order vs. shard-epoch boundaries or (b) backfill ingestion restores older sequences for the same prefix IDs.
root_cause_summary: Aggregation pipelines used two different canonicalization keys: the rate-limiter shard used a shard_epoch + prefix_id alignment (epoch-aligned bucket boundaries), while the billing aggregator used rolling windows keyed by prefix_id + nearest_ingest_minute. When late events (older sequence numbers) were re-ingested, the rate-limiter's shard offset allowed them to be counted into a different bucket than the original event, and the backfill merge stage failed to detect the duplicate because idempotency keys didn't include the shard_epoch. The net result was short-lived duplicate tokens counted in both buckets during the ledger reconstruction window.
steps_taken: Reproduced locally with synthetic late-event generator (see scripts/ingest-sim backfill scenario).

Added verbose tracing to sharder and aggregator to capture (prefix_id, shard_epoch, sequence_no, ingest_time) across pipeline stages — linked traces in Grafana (dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/usage/ingest-trace).
Instrumented a Canary pipeline that runs the compacting merge stage before final aggregation — captured initial reduction of duplicate counts in test traffic.
Opened an initial PR that adds shard_epoch into the idempotency key generation (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8426).
proposed_fix: 1) Canonicalize idempotency keys across sharder and aggregator to include shard_epoch and sequence_uuid; 2) Add an early 'compacting' merge stage in streaming pipeline that deduplicates events with identical (prefix_id, sequence_uuid, shard_epoch) within a 10-minute watermark; 3) Update the aggregation rollback to prefer the earliest ingest_time when a conflict is detected; 4) Add a migration task to re-run recent backfills through the compacting stage for the last 48 hours to remove transient duplicates.
tradeoffs_considered: Increase watermark window to 1 hour would reduce duplicate risk but increase aggregation latency — rejected due to customer SLAs for near-real-time charts.
Canonicalizing to ingest_time only simplifies keys but breaks idempotency when sequence_uuid is present — rejected because sequence_uuid is canonical for ordered prefixes.
Compacting stage increases CPU for streaming workers; chosen approach keeps it small (10-minute keyed compaction) to balance cost and correctness.
next_steps: Finish PR to include shard_epoch in idempotency keys and add unit tests (owner: Liam) — target merge 2026-03-15.
Deploy compacting stage to staging and run synthetic replays (owner: Maya) — staging rollout 2026-03-16.
Run a controlled migration to compact the last 48 hours of ingestion in prod once staging signals green (owner: InfraOps) — migration window 2026-03-18 02:00-05:00 UTC.
Monitor affected customers' charts and billing deltas; prepare rollback plan in case of regressions (owner: SRE).
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate spikes observed in synthetic late-event replay after compacting stage is enabled in staging.
Production canary (5% traffic) shows <=0.1% change in per-model daily totals after migration (acceptable noise threshold), and alerts for duplicates drop to baseline.
PR merged with end-to-end tests that assert idempotency for out-of-order arrivals and shard_epoch transitions.
Migration run completes and backfilled duplicates are reduced to baseline within 24 hours.
Post-mortem written and owners briefed to Console and Billing teams.
